title: Regex trimStrings semantics
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:334 — "| `trimStrings` | Strings stripped from the match |"
reality: Trim strings are removed from the WHOLE resulting text after the replacement runs, every occurrence, whether or not the find pattern matched (not ST's strip-from-the-match semantics). Doc: docs/extending/regex-scripts.md:87 ("strip out after the replacement runs"). Code agrees: packages/server/src/services/regex/regex-application.ts:175-179 and packages/client/src/hooks/use-apply-regex.ts:146-153 run `result.split(trim).join("")` on the full result after applyRegexReplacement. Macros in trim strings resolve first.
fix: custom-tools.md Fields table: change the trimStrings row to "Plain strings deleted from the whole text after the replacement (every occurrence, even when the pattern didn't match; macros resolve) — not SillyTavern's strip-from-match". Add one line warning ST migrants that a broad trim string deletes that text everywhere the script runs.

title: Home Assistant integration mis-described
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:51 — "a first-class Home Assistant integration that **auto-generates webhook custom tools from your HA entities** — you don't hand-write them."
reality: The integration is a HACS custom component installed inside Home Assistant (custom_components/marinara_engine). It upserts a FIXED set of 23 `ha_*` tools in 8 categories (each takes an entity_id or an area/room name), not one tool per entity (custom_components/marinara_engine/const.py:15-34). It also creates a **Home Assistant** agent (type home_assistant, parallel phase, settings.enabledTools; coordinator.py:112-183) that must be added to each chat via Chat Settings → Agents — that is what makes the tools available there (docs/integrations/home-assistant.md:84-92). Locks and Generic Service Calls (Advanced) are off by default; category changes apply only after **Marinara Sync HA Tools**, which disables (not deletes) deselected-category tools and overwrites hand edits (home-assistant.md:104-130, 182-192). A Home Assistant on another device needs IP_ALLOWLIST or ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_PRIVATE_NETWORK=true; BASIC_AUTH blocks it (home-assistant.md:38-46). It also adds HA services marinara_engine.send_message / trigger_generation for automations (home-assistant.md:147-180).
fix: custom-tools.md Home Assistant paragraph: replace "auto-generates webhook custom tools from your HA entities" with "a HACS integration that creates a fixed set of ha_* tools by category (device or room name as the argument) plus a **Home Assistant** agent you add to each chat". Add: Locks/Generic Service Calls off by default; change categories in HA's Configure, then press **Marinara Sync HA Tools** (disables deselected tools, overwrites hand edits — don't edit them in Marinara); remote HA host needs IP_ALLOWLIST (Basic Auth blocks it); automations can push messages in via marinara_engine.send_message. Keep the WEBHOOK_LOCAL_URLS_ENABLED=true note.

title: Theme CSS sanitizer, limits and Theme Library import rules
skill_evidence: absent — references/extensions.md:11-25 (Part 1: Themes) covers native settings and window hooks but never says what the theme sanitizer strips or what limits apply
reality: Theme CSS is cleaned before injection: every url() except data:image/font URIs becomes url(about:invalid), @import and @namespace are stripped, and @font-face survives only if every source is a font data: URI (docs/appearance/custom-css-themes.md:119; code packages/client/src/lib/theme-css.ts:23 → card-css.ts:416-445). Limits: name ≤200 chars, CSS ≤256 KiB measured in UTF-8 bytes (custom-css-themes.md:253-255; packages/shared/src/schemas/theme.schema.ts + css-size.ts MAX_USER_CSS_BYTES). The section is called **Theme Library** (Settings → Addons). A newly created theme saves AND activates; imported .css / .json ({"name","css"}) themes do not auto-activate, and a same-name-same-CSS import is skipped; only one theme is active; **Reset Appearance** turns the active theme off (custom-css-themes.md:47-92). Creating/importing/activating themes from another device needs ADMIN_SECRET + Admin Access (custom-css-themes.md:257-268).
fix: extensions.md Part 1: add a short "What bites in theme CSS" block — remote url()/@import/Google-Fonts links are stripped (embed images/fonts as data: URIs, or add the font natively via Appearance → Text & Scale → Google Fonts / data/fonts); 256 KiB UTF-8 / 200-char name cap; Theme Library import formats and that imports don't auto-activate; Admin Access for remote management. Cite docs/appearance/custom-css-themes.md.

title: Card CSS (Card Theming) surface missing
skill_evidence: absent — references/extensions.md Part 1 presents themes as THE custom-CSS surface; the only Card CSS mention in the skill is the about-me hooks at references/character-cards.md:225
reality: Marinara has a second, independent custom-CSS layer: CSS in a character's (or persona's) **Creator Notes** `<style>` block, switched on per chat in **Chat Settings → Card Theming** (Disabled default / Exclusive / Chat), scoped with `[data-card-css]`, mode-targetable with `@chat-mode roleplay|conversation|game`. Its sanitizer is stricter than a theme's: core tokens such as --primary/--background stripped, !important stripped, position:fixed → absolute, :has() blocked, external url()/@import stripped. Both can be active at once, and either can be the cause when the app looks wrong. Sources: docs/appearance/card-css-theming.md:17-30, 60-77, 101-132, 269-284; docs/appearance/custom-css-themes.md:270-278; en.json:5126 "Card Theming".
fix: extensions.md Part 1: add a 3-5 line "Theme vs. Card CSS" note — a theme repaints the whole app (server-synced, Settings → Addons → Theme Library); Card CSS ships inside a card's Creator Notes, styles only chat messages, must be enabled per chat under Card Theming (default Disabled), and is sanitized more strictly. Route "my character should have its own look" to Card CSS, cross-link character-cards.md, cite docs/appearance/card-css-theming.md.

title: Native Appearance controls that pre-empt custom CSS
skill_evidence: references/extensions.md:15-21 — native-first list names accent, dialogue color, text scale, chat widget style, name colors, Reduce Ambient Animations, Conversation background opacity only
reality: Settings → Appearance also has: **Visual Style** (Default (Marinara) or **SillyTavern**, a minimal ST-like skin — docs/appearance/appearance-settings.md:23-30); **Text Outline / Stroke** (color + 0–5px width) and **Chat Chrome Text Color** (appearance-settings.md:69-76); Roleplay **Chat position** Left/Center/Right on wide screens (new in v2.5.0, #7106 — CHANGELOG-v2.5.0.md:69; appearance-settings.md:95); **Custom Mouse Pointer** (default on — turn it off to use the system cursor or let a theme control the cursor; appearance-settings.md:56-58); **Accent Pulse** / **RGB Mode**, mutually exclusive. All ship in en.json (settings.colors.chatChrome :2738, textOutline :2741, customPointer :2840, roleplayChatPosition :2919, appearancesettings.visualStyle :10255, textOutlineStroke :10249).
fix: extensions.md native-first list: add one line each for Visual Style → SillyTavern (answers "make it look like ST" without a theme), Text Outline/Stroke + Chat Chrome Text Color (readability over busy backgrounds), Chat position (v2.5.0, #7106), and "turn off Custom Mouse Pointer before writing a theme cursor".

title: Chat-style theme variables need the Apply preset switches
skill_evidence: references/extensions.md:23 — theme hooks listed are only window/drawer/bubble classes and --mari-window-* variables
reality: v2.5.0 also exposes chat-area hooks: classes `.mari-chat-style-surface`, `.mari-chat-style-conversation`, `.mari-chat-style-text`, `.mari-chat-style-control` and variables `--mari-chat-font-family`, `--mari-chat-bg`, `--mari-chat-text`, `--mari-chat-border`, `--mari-chat-radius`, `--mari-chat-control-*`, `--mari-chat-input-bg`, plus `--mari-window-font-family`, `--mari-drawer-radius`, `--mari-window-ornament: none`. The --mari-chat-* variables apply through built-in styling ONLY while the matching **Apply preset font/shape/colors** switch is on (docs/appearance/custom-css-themes.md:29, 215-251; code packages/client/src/styles/themes/chat-widget-surfaces.css:76 gates on `:root[data-chat-widget-apply-colors="true"]`).
fix: extensions.md "Theme hooks" paragraph: add the .mari-chat-style-* classes and --mari-chat-* variables with the rule "turn on the matching Apply preset switch or these variables do nothing (or target the classes directly)"; mention --mari-window-ornament: none for hiding the preset title ornament.

title: Regex import skips and validator specifics
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:319-320 — card-embedded ST scripts: unsupported placements kept with a warning; "(v2.4.3) A JSON regex-bundle import now keeps flagged scripts with a warning"; validator described only as rejecting "overlapping broad-unbounded chains"
reality: Regex scripts embedded in a SillyTavern CARD are silently skipped on card import when the pattern is empty, fails the safety check, or won't compile — only the JSON bundle import keeps flagged scripts (docs/extending/regex-scripts.md:159; code packages/server/src/services/import/st-character.importer.ts:146-170 `if (!source || !isPatternSafe(source)) continue;`). Concrete rejection rules: >1000 chars, nested quantifiers like (a+)+, two broad wildcards in a row, three or more broad wildcards anywhere unless delimiter-bounded negated classes (the skill's ([^|]+)\|… example is the exempt case); error "Regex pattern is unsafe: avoid nested quantifiers, ambiguous quantified alternatives, and oversized patterns." A safe script that takes too long on one long message is skipped for that message only and stays enabled (regex-scripts.md:165-178; packages/shared/src/utils/regex-safety.ts:13-26, 305-385; regex-application.ts vmRegexReplaceGuard).
fix: custom-tools.md ReDoS bullet: add "card-embedded ST regexes that fail the check are dropped at card import (rewrite and re-import them via JSON); limits: 1000 chars, no (a+)+, no two adjacent broad wildcards, ≤2 broad wildcards unless delimiter-bounded; a slow script is skipped per message, not disabled."

title: Regex replacement grammar, macros and Live Test
skill_evidence: absent — references/custom-tools.md:313-336 (Regex Scripts section) never mentions replacement tokens, case transforms, macros, or Live Test
reality: Replace With supports $1/$2 captures and case transforms \u$1, \U$1\E, \l$1, \L$1\E (docs/extending/regex-scripts.md:64-73; code packages/shared/src/utils/regex-replacement.ts:9-11 CASE_COMMANDS U/L/E/u/l). Macros such as {{user}}/{{char}} resolve in Find (as literal text), Replace and Trim Strings (regex-scripts.md:93; use-apply-regex.ts:141-152). **Live Test** previews find/replace/trim only — not placement, enabled state, scope or depth (regex-scripts.md:89-91).
fix: custom-tools.md Regex section: add one bullet — "Replace supports $n and \u/\U…\E/\l/\L…\E case transforms; {{user}}/{{char}} macros work in find (literal), replace and trim; Live Test checks the pattern only, not placement/scope/depth" — useful when porting ST scripts that use {{char}}.

title: Ruleset reroll/spend limits misstated
skill_evidence: references/rulesets.md:30 — "`reroll` (≤6 free re-throws), plus `spend` (≤4 paid purchases of successes, dice or a re-throw; pool-only, and refused on `dice-sum`)"
reality: `resolution.reroll` is up to six named re-throw RULES ({id, upTo, mode once|until}); a check names one with reroll= and throws at most one re-throw (docs/extending/writing-rulesets.md:134). `resolution.spend` is up to four spend RULES, no two on the same pool; each rule's purchases per check are capped by `perCheck` (1–10, a sheet value, or "pool"), so a check can make up to perCheck purchases per rule, not 4 in total (writing-rulesets.md:175-187). Schema: packages/shared/src/schemas/ruleset.schema.ts:355 `spend: z.array(...).max(4)`, :480-483 reroll `.max(6)`, :303-316 perCheck.
fix: rulesets.md:30: reword to "`reroll` (≤6 named free re-throw rules; one per check), plus `spend` (≤4 rules, one per pool, each buying successes, dice or a re-throw up to `perCheck` purchases per check; pool-only, refused on dice-sum)".

title: Agent-attached tools don't need the chat's Enable Tool Use
skill_evidence: references/custom-tools.md:288-290 — "Tools attach to a specific agent as well as to a chat … that's how a custom agent gains a callable capability." (silent on whether Enable Tool Use is required)
reality: Code: an agent's settings.enabledTools are resolved even when the chat's Enable Tool Use is off — packages/server/src/services/generation/tool-resolution-runtime.ts:895-905 (`resolveTools: enableChatTools || enableAgentTools || …`), :1106-1124 (agent tool list built from allToolDefs), :1290-1296 (resolveAgentGenerationTools passes enableChatTools:false). docs/integrations/home-assistant.md:92 matches the code ("You do not need to turn anything else on in the chat"); docs/extending/custom-tools.md:163 says the opposite ("you still turn on Enable Tool Use") — that doc lags.
fix: custom-tools.md "Attaching tools to an agent": add "An agent uses its attached tools in its own call whether or not the chat's Enable Tool Use is on (docs/extending/custom-tools.md says otherwise; the code and the Home Assistant doc agree it isn't needed). Enable Tool Use governs the main narrator's tools."

title: Personal Extension re-import/update lifecycle
skill_evidence: references/extensions.md:42 — "re-importing a byte-identical package keeps its approval, while changed executable content clears it"; extensions.md:262 distribution checklist
reality: Re-importing an extension with the same name UPDATES the existing record after a confirmation ("Replace the saved code for … with this local file? The extension will be disabled and require approval of its new hash." — en.json:10463), and numeric dotted `config.version` values trigger an **Import Older Revision?** downgrade warning (en.json:10452; docs/extending/writing-personal-extensions.md:205, 233). There is no URL installer, remote catalog or automatic updater — every update is a manual re-import plus fresh hash approval (docs/development/personal-extensions.md:19). Delete removes the record and its private settings; export first (writing-personal-extensions.md:237; development/personal-extensions.md:47).
fix: extensions.md (approval paragraph or Recovery): add "Re-import under the same name to update — Marinara confirms the replacement, disables it for re-approval, and warns on a lower numeric `config.version`. No URL installer or auto-updater exists, so distributing updates means recipients re-import and re-approve." Mirror the update loop in the advising checklist item 5.
